headline: Secure Guest Ranch and Forest Stays in the Wind River Valley
reservation: Dubois glamping and guest ranch stays often book six months to a year in advance for the July-August peak. While no federal permits are required for the town itself, backcountry access in the Shoshone National Forest may involve specific grazing or group permits. Changing systems for wilderness entry require an official check with the US Forest Service.

days.title: Bighorn Sheep and Badlands

stops.name: National Bighorn Sheep Center
stops.detail: Learn about the Whiskey Basin herd and local conservation efforts before heading into the field.

stops.name: Dubois Badlands
stops.detail: Explore the striking red rock formations and lunar-like clay hills east of town.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for local exploration; conditions vary
days.note: Early season visitors should be prepared for muddy roads in the badlands.

days.title: Absaroka Alpine Lakes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Wind River Valley

stops.name: Lake Louise Trailhead
stops.detail: A moderate ascent into the mountains offering views of glacial carved valleys and alpine water.

stops.name: Shoshone National Forest
stops.detail: Traverse the high-altitude pine forests and look for signs of local elk and moose.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for forest access roads; conditions vary
days.note: Bear-proof food storage is mandatory in this region; check current forest alerts.

days.title: Togwotee High Country

stops.name: Togwotee Pass
stops.detail: Experience the dramatic views of the Teton Range from this high mountain pass.

stops.name: Brooks Lake
stops.detail: Visit this scenic alpine lake beneath the Pinnacle Buttes for photography and light walking.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours for mountain pass travel; conditions vary
days.note: Snow can block high passes through June; verify road status with WYDOT.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Popular spots like Lake Louise have limited spaces that fill early during summer weekends. Have a secondary lower-elevation trail in mind if primary lots are full.

intel.title: Deep Valley Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly unreliable once you leave the US-286 corridor toward the mountains. Download offline maps and notify others of your route before departing town.

intel.title: Town Supply Hub
intel.text: Dubois serves as the final fuel and grocery stop before crossing Togwotee Pass toward the national parks. Ensure tanks are full before heading into the Shoshone backcountry.

intel.title: High Altitude Pace
intel.text: Most high-country trails are only snow-free from July through early September. Plan for slower hiking speeds if you are not acclimated to the 7,000+ foot elevation.

intel.title: Forest Road Conditions
intel.text: Unpaved forest roads can become impassable after afternoon thunderstorms in July. Check with the ranger station for the current status of roads leading to Brooks Lake.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Central Wyoming Regional Airport and pick up a rental. Stop in Riverton for major supplies before the 80-minute drive to your Dubois base.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance 4WD is recommended for unpaved forest roads; check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Pinnacles at Brooks Lake offer spectacular light at sunset, though shadows fall early in the deep valleys.
